12. Mr. Khan Tipu Sultan, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners submits, that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal; that the Court of appeal below did not consider the points which were raised and decided by the Trial Court; that the findings of the Appellate Court are based on surmise and conjecture and not on evidence on record; that the Appellate Court in deciding the appeal did not applied its judicial mind, nor Consider the map of the union, view of the majority people and the decision of this Court reported in 15 MLR (AD) 230, and also failed to appreciate Article 111 of Constitution of the Republic; that the Appellate Court without proper consideration of law and facts just on surmise and conjecture arrived into its wrong decision based on wrong findings which occasioned failure of justice. He further submits, that the Deputy Commissioner i.e. the Government selected the place of construction of the Union Parishad Complex and he has reported about his such selection and his such report cannot be questioned as being in violation of the Rules of business; that selection and shifting of Union Parishad Office is a Government policy and decision and the plaintiffs have got no legal character and locus stand to challenge such decision, and as such the suit is not maintainable as it held by the Trial Court. Mr. Khan Tipu Sultan further submits that on 28.12.2005 the government has issued a circular providing guideline regarding selection of place for constructing Union Parishad Complex, and such Government's circular has got compulsive effect in between its maker and persons upon whom the same is applicable. In support, he cited the decisions in the 'cases of Golam Mortuza Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 47, Mr. Abdul Motaleb Sarker and others Vs. Mr. Laskar Ali and others reported in 15 MLR (AD) 231, and Ezahar Ali Mondol and others vs. Golam Rasul and others reported in 45 DLR 653. 

 13. In reply of his such argument, Mr. Tabarak Hossain, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiffs/opposite parties submits, that the Trial Court committed illegality in deciding the issues framed in the suit in negative, but the Appellate Court on proper consideration of materials on record rightly set aside the judgment of the Trial Court and on reversal of the same decreed the suit.
